title: Tomas heads out of the harbour (paraphrase C)
topic: A fisherman named Tomas works a day at sea from a small harbour; nets, gulls, the catch, the market
tail_E: At home that evening the family eats fresh
target_note: Same target as formulations A and B: 'fish' is predictable only from the context (nets let down into the water, a heavy day's take arranged in tubs and taken by buyers); the units speak of 'the day's take' / 'die Ausbeute' and 'the catch' / 'der Fang' and never of fish. notes: Formulation C: third independent re-phrasing of the ten meaning units of F02A in both languages (same events, same order, same name Tomas, wording different from A and B). 'boat' is kept as 'Boot' with a different subject phrase, 'harbour' / 'Hafen' is kept (no common synonym), the catch becomes 'the day's take' / 'die Ausbeute' in unit 7 and 'the catch' / 'der Fang' in unit 9. Unit 2 'stampft' is the nautical verb for pitching; unit 4 'lässt die Netze ins eisige Wasser' (lets the nets down) has no verb particle; unit 5 'zieht Kreise' (draws circles) for 'circle'; unit 8 'hält Ausschau nach ihm' (keeps a lookout for him) for 'waits'; unit 9 'übernehmen' (inseparable) for 'buy'; unit 10 'draws to a close in harbour' / 'findet sein Ende im Hafen' for 'ends at the harbour' ('in harbour' is the nautical phrase without article). No separable verbs. Unit 9 reads naturally in German; units 1 and 10 read naturally in English.
